description: Plot GO term distribution across PIAS subfamilies
code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
terms=["SUMO ligase activity\n(GO:0061665, F)","protein sumoylation\n(GO:0016925, P)","chromatin\n(GO:0000785, C)",
"transcription coregulator\n(GO:0003712, F)","reg. transcription Pol II\n(GO:0006357, P)","nuclear receptor coactivator*\n(GO:0030374, F, OBSOLETE)"]
freq=[25,25,25,9,9,3]
colors=["#2c7fb8","#2c7fb8","#d95f02","#7570b3","#7570b3","#999999"]
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,4.5))
b=ax.barh(terms[::-1],freq[::-1],color=colors[::-1])
ax.axvline(25,ls="--",c="gray",lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("Number of subfamilies with this GO term (of 25)")
ax.set_title("PTHR10782 (PIAS): GO terms are mapped at SUBFAMILY level\nParent family entry itself has ZERO GO terms")
for i,v in enumerate(freq[::-1]): ax.text(v+0.2,i,str(v),va="center")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("pias_go_distribution.png",dpi=120)
print("saved")
print("Universal (25/25): SUMO ligase activity, protein sumoylation, chromatin")
print("Metazoan-restricted (9/25): transcription coregulator, reg Pol II transcription")
print("3/25 obsolete term: nuclear receptor coactivator")
